events.title: Heraclius restores the True Cross to Jerusalem
events.description: By tradition on this day, Emperor Heraclius returned the relic of the cross, captured by the Persians in 614, to Jerusalem. Within a decade the city fell to the Arab armies.
events.html: By tradition on this day, Emperor Heraclius returned the relic of the cross, captured by the Persians in 614, to Jerusalem. Within a decade the city fell to the Arab armies.

events.title: Thomas Cranmer burned at the stake in Oxford
events.description: The former Archbishop of Canterbury, author of the Book of Common Prayer, withdrew his recantations before Mary I's officials. He thrust the hand that had signed them into the flames first.
events.html: The former Archbishop of Canterbury, author of the Book of Common Prayer, withdrew his recantations before Mary I's officials. He thrust the hand that had signed them into the flames first.

events.title: Great fire destroys much of New Orleans
events.description: A Good Friday fire burned 856 buildings in the Spanish colonial city. With a second fire in 1794, it led to the rebuilding of the French Quarter in brick and tile.
events.html: A Good Friday fire burned 856 buildings in the Spanish colonial city. With a second fire in 1794, it led to the rebuilding of the French Quarter in brick and tile.

events.title: Pius VII crowned pope in Venice
events.description: With Rome occupied by the French, the cardinals met in Venice, where Barnaba Chiaramonti was crowned Pope Pius VII. He later signed a concordat with Napoleon and was held captive by him.
events.html: With Rome occupied by the French, the cardinals met in Venice, where Barnaba Chiaramonti was crowned Pope Pius VII. He later signed a concordat with Napoleon and was held captive by him.

events.title: Germany launches its Spring Offensive
events.description: Operation Michael struck British lines on the Somme after a five-hour bombardment, gaining more ground in days than any attack since 1914. It ran out of steam, and the Allies counter-attacked that summer.

events.title: Police kill 69 protesters at Sharpeville
events.description: South African police fired on an unarmed crowd protesting against the pass laws, killing 69 people. The government banned the ANC and PAC, and 21 March is now Human Rights Day in South Africa.
